candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.8, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Apply principles of infection prevention; Educate client and staff regarding infection-prevention measures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — duration of Transmission-Based Precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Use pathogen- and condition-specific CDC criteria to determine the duration of Transmission-Based Precautions rather than applying a universal stopping time.

options.A: Continue Droplet Precautions indefinitely because pathogen-specific stopping criteria do not exist.
options.B: Stop Droplet Precautions exactly 24 hours after they begin for every respiratory infection, regardless of the diagnosis or clinical course.
options.C: Use the organism- and condition-specific duration criteria in current infection-control guidance, because precautions continue while transmission risk persists and the required duration varies by infection.
options.D: Discontinue precautions whenever the client requests it, regardless of transmission risk, treatment status, or infection-control guidance.

candidate.rationale: CDC states that Transmission-Based Precautions remain in effect while risk for transmission persists and that the duration depends on the infectious agent and condition. Appendix A gives pathogen-specific durations—for example, some Droplet Precautions continue until 24 hours after effective therapy, whereas others continue for the duration of illness or according to other criteria. Therefore C is correct. A, B, and D incorrectly apply an indefinite, universal 24-hour, or preference-based rule.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Transmission-Based Precautions continue while transmission risk persists, and duration varies by pathogen/condition according to current CDC guidance.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — III. Precautions to Prevent Transmission of Infectious Agents; Appendix A: Type and Duration of Precautions Recommended for Selected Infections and Conditions

candidate.stem: A client is receiving Droplet Precautions for a respiratory infection. How should the nurse determine when the Transmission-Based Precautions can be discontinued?
